units.en: As ⟦0⟧ liberate all native people in North and South America.
Mapuche Chile
Strategy

This achievement essentially requires complete control of the American continent, from Greenland to Uruguay. Subjects count, and holding the territory is not necessary once the nation has been released. A complication is that four countries have to either be your subject or not exist at all to unlock the decision, which means going to the peace conference: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧. Pacific nations like, Hawaii, Samoa, or Tahiti don't have to be released.
USA
Canada
Brazil
Bolivia

To successfully puppet a country in the peace conference, you must puppet its capital region and make sure that none of its territory remains unclaimed at the end of the conference. Otherwise, your puppet will be an entirely new nation and the original country will not be considered your subject. You know you have succeeded if your puppet uses the original country's focus tree.

On old versions of the game, it was possible to invite Brazil into your faction (this may still be possible with ⟦0⟧ disabled) and then rush the Allies down before the US joined. The strategy here previously used this method. This doesn't work after the free patch that came with ⟦1⟧, as the UK defends their shores relentlessly with a large army garrison and the Royal Navy.
No Compromise, No Surrender

While the current strategy listed here does this with historical AI focuses, it is possible to reroll for a good non-historical run where the UK decolonizes (or even better, disbands the Allies by joining the Axis or Comintern). If the following strategy doesn't work for you, try that.

As a final note, there are two strategies on how to do this run in essence, and both are very viable. One strategy has you immediately take the decisions to release puppets and to abuse manpower and troops offered by puppets to supplement your own meager reserves. In this strategy, you would take the advisors that give "+ Monthly Population %" and "+ Max Factories in State %". Those modifiers would help turbocharge your economy and manpower base. However, there is an alternative strategy preferred by some players. In that version of the run, you never release or puppet anything until right at the very end of the run after you peace out with the Allies with all the territory you need. You directly annex all land and use the "+ Non-core manpower %" advisors. These advisors are incredibly strong and scale very well, but you have to deal with the logistics and possible resistance issues from garrisoning two entire continents directly. This page details how to do the first strategy here. If you want more details on doing the second version, look at "Method 1" listed for ⟦0⟧. It briefly summarizes it.
Chilean Empire
Civil War

Train your navy, and use your initial Navy Experience to design either an Early Destroyer or Basic Submarine variant with all the modules maxed out with your current technology. Put all but one of your ⟦0⟧ on these and the last one on convoys. Use the destroyers in combination with stolen fleets from other countries to threaten the Allied fleets later. Use the submarines later in the game to raid Allies' convoys and cripple their trade.

Address the Mapuche Conflict

It's generally worth it to do most focuses in this civil war section, as they are all locked out afterwards and almost all of them give permanent buffs. However, if you skip 2 focuses here, you'll bypass the timed event where Ibáñez sells your northernmost core to ⟦0⟧. This actually makes the civil war slightly harder, since this effectively doubles Ibáñez's Military factory count by letting him keep that extra core. However, it makes the build-up to fight Argentina afterwards easier, since you have an extra Military factory. As to which focuses to skip, pick two out of: Unión Araucana, La Corporación Araucana, and Undermine the Carabineros de Chile.

Cooperate with the ⟦0⟧ in the First Congress event. This unlocks incredible advisors, so it's worth the 10% Stability hit. Be careful: Ibáñez remains your leader until you have completed Avenge the Pacification of Araucanía, and the communists will start their own civil war against you if they reach over 20% popularity while he is in charge. If you want to do Red Hot Chile Peppers afterwards, the decision for a referendum will appear once you reach at least 60% communist support at any point in the run from now on. The communist leader is generally weaker than your second leader option (Esteban Romero Sandoval) in direct combat scenarios, but he's better than the other two options, especially in terms of stability. If you are struggling severely with stability later on, switching to Communist may help you a lot.

There's a lot of variance in the civil war, as the AI can defend certain mountain tiles very well. Try for encirclements on the most well-defended tiles. Make sure to promote your high level General with Organizer into a Field Marshal and take the max planning bonus trait; it will help. If unable to progress, consider sending two naval invasions of 2-width cavalry divisions, each hitting as many different tiles on the enemy coastline as possible. This will force them to pull about half their troops off the line, which gives you the momentum back. The enemy has more factories than you, allowing you to grab Extensive Conscription. In theory, you can also get War Economy. However, with no coal access, making yourself heavily reliant on easily raided convoys to keep your economy active is risky. It's safer to stay on Partial Mobilization. This civil war also counts as a defensive war. In theory, that would allow you to take Desperate Defense. However, you will very likely not have enough army experience for that. The civil war ends once you've pushed to Coquimbo.

War with Argentina
Argentina has more men and industry than you and should be rushed as fast as reasonably possible. However, you also need to prepare for war with Brazil at the same time.
Put out 20 12-width infantries, preferably also with Support Artillery. Also put out 12 6-width cavalry divisions.
Put them both on the ⟦0⟧ border as individual general frontlines, not as a field marshal order. Don't forget to put a couple troops on Terra del Fuego.
Argentine

Optional (but recommended): rush first towards ⟦0⟧. You desperately need a third research slot just to keep up in regular technologies. Nevermind the fact that we will need at minimum a navy and tanks for later. I recommend taking the Dissolve COVENSA path. It seems worse on the surface than the alternative path, but you will quickly find that you have enough building slots anyway to nearly max out your major cores just from the two different advisors that grant Max Factories % and Monthly Population %, who you should be using. And that tiny bit of Steel makes a huge difference. As an aside, don't bother taking Establish Beneficial Trade Relationships until much, much later (after the US is conquered, ideally); the focus is basically pure downside at first, with a long-term gain of some moderate economy buffs after you take International Loans, improve relations with major powers, and dump in huge amounts of Political Power. But the additional forced Resources to Market % at the start will force you to depend on external trading partners like Sweden even more than you already need to. The Allies will raid your convoys and starve you.

Take the "Improve Worker Conditions" decision every time you can for the rest of the playthrough. It doesn't matter if you're at war, or how badly you might need your factories; you will be starved of stability in this run basically from the start to the finish.
The Union of American Indigenous Peoples
After completing ⟦0⟧, use your Faction Initiative point to declare yourself Head of Cryptology, Counter Intelligence, or Operations. This gives you an additional spy.

Use your two spies to start a Collaboration Government on ⟦0⟧. If you were unlucky, you may have to first rescue your original spy. Work towards getting your third spy via completing 5 agency upgrades. When you have this, you can set your Collaboration Government operation to automatically repeat and the third spy can hold the Network Level in Brazil above the 50% Threshold required, so the operation will repeat seamlessly. You can quiet the network as well with this third spy to reduce the chance of detection once you've past the threshold.

When you declare war, pin the Argentinian divisions with attacks while your cavalry divisions encircle them and rush victory points. Getting Buenos Aires is crucial. Before the war, you can set up a naval invasion order for 6 of the cavalry divisions to naval invade Buenos Aires. If you wait a few days after the war starts to launch the naval invasion, you may get it for free because the AI pulled its garrison out of desperation. In the peace deal, take all of your cores from Argentina. Puppet the remaining states while taking their civilian factories and resources. Also take their navy.

War with Brazil

Non-fascist countries will join the Allies when they reach a certain surrender progress after a certain amount of world tension has accumulated. This is a problem because a fight with the Allies and Brazil simultaneously will waste huge amounts of your time, which is a limited resource. You're on an invisible clock to at least take Mexico and parts of the US before Sweden joins the Allies (typically mid-1942 when doing this). When that happens, you'll lose your source of Steel for your armies' Infantry Equipment.

However, there's a trick: the countries above only join the Allies when they near defeat (unless you are already at war with the Allies). If you manipulate their surrender progress such that they pass that trigger at the same time they capitulate, they don't have time to join a faction (in theory... in practice, the "lag" before a country actually capitulates can sometimes allow them to join a faction anyway). This is why we wanted the Collaboration Governments on Brazil. (Additionally, if this strategy fails, you can form a Collaboration Government in occupied Brazil in order to not have to garrison it, so you get a big benefit either way.)
